basis: Visual estimate from scheme-a-adventurous.png against scheme-a-2045.png. This board is the loosest geometric interpretation, so the plate controls all massing, field and water boundaries.

roofMix.reading: Across the whole scheme, new homes are PV-led, campus blocks mix planted and PV roofs, and existing suburbs remain slate and tile. Walkable roof paths are visible mainly on the large courtyard blocks.

wallMaterials.material: warm buff brick and low-carbon masonry

windowRhythm.storeyHeightMetres: 2.9 to 3.1 for homes; 3.3 to 3.5 for campus
windowRhythm.windowWidthMetres: 0.9 to 1.2 on terraces; 1.9 to 2.4 within 3 m campus bays
windowRhythm.windowProportion: Tall domestic openings around 0.6 width:height; campus glazing around 1.4 to 1.7 width:height
windowRhythm.revealDepthImpression: About 200 mm on masonry homes and 350 to 500 mm behind the campus timber frame.
windowRhythm.rhythm: Domestic party-wall cadence on the left; strong horizontal floor bands and vertical timber posts on the right. Avoid one facade rule across both.

groundCover.hardLandscapeColour: #A79B84 buff public paths and #60615C asphalt roads
groundCover.reading: The whole scheme is held together by woodland, gardens and a wetland spine. Hard landscape is concentrated at streets and campus thresholds rather than spread as plazas.

water.visible: A narrow sinuous foreground brook, a connected chain of shallow ponds and rain gardens through the central woodland, and smaller campus channels.
water.channelWidthMetres: 2 to 5, locally 6 to 8 where the channel ponds
water.pondSize: Main basins roughly 20 to 45 m across, with smaller rain-garden pockets
water.reflectivity: Silver-blue sky reflection, #8CA5A9 lit and #2D4B4E shaded, interrupted heavily by reed beds and tree shadow.
water.buildability: The board makes the stream wider and invents some ponds. Keep the surveyed brook narrow and place added open water only where the wetland class and drainage logic support it.

trees.density: High in the central woodland and orchard ring, medium in streets and courts, deliberately open over wet meadow and panel fields.
trees.arrangement: Large irregular central woodland with clearings, rectilinear orchards, disciplined avenues through built parcels, isolated veteran trees in courts, and lower wetland species following water.

sustainableFeatures.PVGlint: Blue-black #17242E with sparse cool highlights #91A4AB. Use consistent row orientation and keep glint directional, not a blanket brightness increase.
sustainableFeatures.canopies: Solar carports are visible around GCHQ and selected parking, elevated on slim posts with cars or asphalt visible beneath.
sustainableFeatures.agrivoltaicRows: Vertical bifacial 2 m rows in the left fields at about 10 to 12 m centres. Most of the field must remain green.
sustainableFeatures.glasshouses: Small distant pale glass volumes north of the panel fields. Read through fine frames and sky reflections, never as opaque white sheds.
sustainableFeatures.other: Campus meadow roofs, walkable roof loops, productive orchards and the connected wetland spine should all read in one glance.

people/vehicles.people: Small figures along the main wetland path, campus entries and a few accessible roofs. They are near the limit of useful resolution at 450 m.
people/vehicles.vehicles: Sparse moving traffic, parked cars in recognised parking areas and beneath carports. Avoid populating every road.
people/vehicles.scopeNote: At this wide camera, people are not buildable as meaningful 3D detail. If required, use sparse stable sprites after all landscape and roof work.

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate reads as large empty olive parcels between isolated building bands; the board reads as a continuous inhabited landscape of woodland, orchards, gardens and wetland.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Break broad classes into parcel-scale garden, meadow, orchard and wetland zones, then soften their boundaries while preserving the masterplan geometry.
gapsVsPlate.system: scripts/golden_valley_2045.py and gv-2045 land-cover data, rendered by future.js
gapsVsPlate.effort: 1 to 1.5 days, largely covered by in-flight M5

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate tree mass is sparse and uniformly faceted; the board's central woodland and orchard ring are the dominant organising structure.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Create distinct veteran, woodland, avenue, orchard and wetland forms; cluster woodland, regularise orchards and deepen shaded canopy values.
gapsVsPlate.system: tree geometry/grade in landcover.js and future.js, plus gv-2045 tree data
gapsVsPlate.effort: 1.5 to 2 days, covered by in-flight M5

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate barely reveals water; the board has a continuous reflective brook and pond sequence through the centre.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Keep the brook narrow but improve reflectivity, add only drainage-supported ponded reaches and blend reed margins into wet meadow.
gapsVsPlate.system: ground shader in future.js, water in life.js and generated land-cover data

gapsVsPlate.difference: Plate roofs are a limited dark or green palette; the board makes PV, meadow and walkable roof programmes visibly different across homes and campus.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Set typology-specific roof allocation to the target mix and strengthen module, meadow and path masks so each reads at 450 m.
gapsVsPlate.system: roof shader in facades.js and roof programme in scripts/golden_valley_2045.py

gapsVsPlate.difference: The plate's large blocks are flat beige grids; the board has honey timber depth, dark glazing and warm masonry variation.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Use separate campus and home material grades, deepen campus reveals and introduce deterministic block-level variation without adding facade geometry beyond the visible bay grid.
gapsVsPlate.system: futureGeometry in future.js, facade materials in facades.js and KEYED_GRADE

gapsVsPlate.difference: Agrivoltaics are flat ground stripes in the plate and elevated energy infrastructure in the board.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Build instanced vertical panel rows with posts, terrain following, narrow shadows and green spacing.
gapsVsPlate.system: scripts/golden_valley_2045.py data and futureGeometry in future.js

gapsVsPlate.difference: The board shifts housing rows, courtyard dimensions, woodland clearings and pond positions well beyond the requested tolerance.
gapsVsPlate.modellingAction: Do not reproduce board geometry drift. Use shots.json and the plate as the camera and layout master, and treat the board as a character, density and palette reference only.
